title: Paul Robeson's birth chart
metaDescription: Paul Robeson's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.9° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 19.9° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 19.9° Aries: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is the Sun. A fire sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 9.2° Taurus, Venus was at 3.0° Taurus, Mars was at 15.2° Pisces. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun sextile Neptune, 0.3° of separation. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Uranus at 0.4°, and Saturn opposition Pluto at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Saturn opposes Pluto while both square Mars. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aries at 19.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Taurus at 3.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 3 in fire, 3 in air, 2 in earth, 1 in water by element, 5 mutable, 2 cardinal, 2 fixed by modality. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.6° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
